title: MINT: Mitigating Structural Inconsistency via Attentive Message Passing for Financial Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.34950v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Illicit account detection is a critical task for financial risk control systems, aiming to pinpoint malicious actors within transaction networks. Existing efforts typically recast transaction networks into directed multigraphs and leverage graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect anomalies via topological structures under the homophily assumption. However, directly grafting GNNs onto transaction graphs is faced with at least two pivotal challenges, i.e., structural inconsistency and label scarcity. The former arises from deceptive connections forged by malicious actors, while the latter stems from the lack of annotated data. In light of these, we introduce MINT, a novel graph neural framework that mitigates structural inconsistency via an attentive message-passing scheme on transaction graphs. translated_title: MINT：基于注意力消息传递机制缓解结构不一致性的金融异常检测方法
translated_abstract: 非法账户检测是金融风控系统中的一项关键任务，旨在精确定位交易网络中的恶意行为者。现有研究通常将交易网络重构为有向多重图，并在同质性假设下利用图神经网络（GNN）通过拓扑结构来检测异常。然而，直接将GNN嫁接到交易图上至少面临两个关键挑战，即结构不一致性和标签稀缺性。前者源于恶意行为者伪造的欺骗性连接，后者则源于标注数据的缺乏。鉴于此，我们提出了MINT，这是一种新颖的图神经框架，通过在交易图上采用注意力消息传递机制来缓解结构不一致性问题。具体而言，MINT引入了一种差异感知的特征传播方法，通过量化节点之间的偏差来追踪恶意行为者……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了MINT图神经框架，通过差异感知的特征传播和注意力消息传递机制来缓解交易网络中由恶意伪造连接造成的结构不一致性问题，从而提升非法账户的检测效果。
en_tdlr: MINT is a novel graph neural framework that mitigates structural inconsistency in transaction graphs through discrepancy-aware feature propagation and attentive message passing, thereby improving illicit account detection.
